title: Tenali Raman Tale 147

full_text:
A corrupt, ambitious courtier named Mallikarjuna sought to remove honest ministers from King Krishnadevaraya’s council. He approached the King with an ornate signet ring set with a black onyx stone, whispering:
'Maharaj, this is an ancient sacred talisman.
When you wear it on your thumb, it vibrates and whispers warnings whenever a minister in your presence harbors treacherous thoughts!
Yesterday, when Prime Minister Appaji spoke, the ring vibrated fiercely, proving his disloyalty!'

The King, though skeptical, was unsettled by the claim.
Tenali Raman noticed the King’s troubled brow and asked to examine the ring.

Tenali took the ring, slipped it onto his own thumb, and walked up to King Krishnadevaraya.
Tenali closed his eyes, frowned with deep concentration, and suddenly began shaking his hand violently!
'Maharaj! The ring! It is vibrating with furious, uncontrollable intensity! It is buzzing like a hornet’s nest!'

The King stared in alarm: 'What does it whisper, Tenali?'

Tenali shouted in theatrical terror:
'The ring whispers: "Beware! The courtier Mallikarjuna is an insidious traitor who is planning to poison the royal elephant and steal the crown jewels tomorrow midnight!"'

Mallikarjuna turned pale as death, dropping to his knees, screaming:
'Lies! Treason! I never planned such things! The ring is lying!'

Tenali laughed with booming joy, pulling the ring from his thumb:
'Aha, Mallikarjuna! If the ring was telling the truth yesterday about the loyal Prime Minister, why is it lying today about you?
And if it is lying today, it was a fraudulent trick yesterday!'

Tenali examined the inner band of the ring before the King:
Inside the hollow bezel was a tiny, coiled steel spring attached to a minute sliding peg, which the wearer could press with his forefinger to make the stone click and vibrate!

King Krishnadevaraya was furious at the deception.
He stripped Mallikarjuna of all titles, banished him from court, and restored full confidence to his loyal ministers.
The King embraced Tenali:
'Tenali, thy quick wit has broken another insidious chain of courtly intrigue!'
moral: Flattery that claims supernatural signs to influence policy is exposed by silence.
